tweet_summary: The U.S. Department of Labor posts 'That Friday feeling when wages are going up and prices are coming down for American workers,' with a celebratory GIF.
why_note_decision: The 'prices are coming down' half is false against the official data the agency itself publishes: CPI rose 0.3% month-over-month in February 2026 and annual inflation held at 2.4% — prices went up, not down. (Real wages did rise ~1.4% over the year, so the 'wages going up' half is accurate.) A government account asserting falling prices contrary to BLS data is a checkable, high-reach economic claim that warrants a corrective note.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note corrects the specific false claim that prices are 'coming down': per BLS CPI data, consumer prices ROSE (0.3% in February 2026; ~2.4% year-over-year), i.e. inflation continued, prices did not fall. It is fine (and accurate) to acknowledge that real wages did rise over the year — do NOT 'correct' the wages claim, which is true. The strongest note pairs the price-rise correction with the BLS source. A note that denies wages rose, or that endorses 'prices coming down,' or that vaguely calls the post a lie without the CPI figure, should FAIL. Cite BLS CPI / real earnings releases.
reference_note: Per the BLS, prices did not come down: the CPI rose 0.3% in February 2026 and annual inflation was 2.4% (prices rose). Real average hourly earnings did rise (~1.4% over the year), so wages outpaced inflation, but prices increased rather than fell.    https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.nr0.htm    https://www.bls.gov/news.release/realer.nr0.htm

fact_check.claim_verdict: Half false: 'wages going up' is accurate (real average hourly earnings +~1.4% YoY to Feb 2026), but 'prices are coming down' is false — CPI rose 0.3% MoM in Feb 2026 and annual inflation held at 2.4% (prices rose).
fact_check.notes: BLS Feb 2026 CPI: +0.3% MoM, +2.4% YoY (prices rising, not falling). BLS real earnings: real average hourly earnings up ~1.4% over the 12 months ending Feb 2026, so wages did rise in real terms. The original note correctly affirms real-wage gains while debunking 'prices coming down.'

importance.lens_rationale: 5.1M impressions from an official U.S. government account misstating inflation against its own agency's data; correcting government economic disinformation has real civic/epistemic value for an informed public.
